inline_comments.comment: `width` and `height` are not valid SVG attributes for a `<circle>` element — a circle's size is defined solely by its `r` attribute. These two `.attr()` calls have no visual effect and should be removed.

Three parameters of `drawCentralConnection` are never read inside the function body: `msgModel` (line 287), `startx` (line 288), and `stopx` (line 289). Actor center positions are recomputed from `diagObj.db.getActors()` instead. Remove the dead parameters from the signature (and update the call site at the corresponding `drawMessage` invocation) to avoid misleading callers.

`bounds.newActivation()` is called for both `CENTRAL_CONNECTION` (line 1018) and `CENTRAL_CONNECTION_REVERSE` (line 1021) signals. `newActivation` draws an activation bar on the actor, which is the correct behaviour for `ACTIVE_START` but is semantically wrong for a central-connection circle marker. These two cases should not activate actors; they should either be no-ops (if the circle rendering is handled entirely inside `drawCentralConnection`) or use a dedicated bounds update that does not create an activation box.

`.attr('stroke', 'black')` hardcodes the stroke colour for the stick arrowhead marker. All other arrow markers in this file (e.g. `insertArrowHead`, `insertArrowCrossHead`) omit an explicit stroke so they inherit the theme's `--mermaid-edge-color` or the diagram's CSS. Hardcoding `'black'` means stick arrowheads will be invisible or incorrect in dark themes. Use `'context-stroke'` (SVG 2 contextual fill/stroke) or omit the attribute and rely on CSS, matching the approach used for the solid markers.
Same hardcoded `stroke: 'black'` issue as in `insertStickTopArrowHead` — `insertStickBottomArrowHead` will also ignore the active theme colour.
The trailing comment `//final_4.11` on the ACTOR token regex appears to be a development annotation left over from iterative work. Remove it before merging.

`activate: true` is set on the `addMessage` payload for the `actor signaltype '()' actor` rule (and similarly on the dual rule at line 343). In the existing grammar, actor activation is handled exclusively by a separate `activeStart` signal — the `activate` field on `addMessage` is never set to `true` in regular signal rules. Setting it here is inconsistent and could mislead future readers or a future consumer of the `activate` field. Use `activate: false` (or omit it to take the default) to match the convention for non-activation messages.

Tests named `'1 should parse'` and `'2 should parse'` (lines 2316 and 2335) call `diagram.db.getMessages()` but make no assertions on the result. A test that can never fail provides no regression value. Add concrete `expect(messages).toHaveLength(...)` and `expect(messages[x]).toMatchObject(...)` assertions as is done in the adjacent `'Central Connection Parsing'` describe block.

Test names `'1 should parse '` and `'2 should parse '` (note the trailing space) are neither descriptive nor professional. Replace with names that specify what is being parsed and what is expected, for example `'should parse all eight half-arrow types'` and `'should parse bidirectional central connection syntax'`.

`docs/` is auto-generated by the docs-build pipeline and its files carry a header warning against direct edits. This file was edited directly: a ```` ```mermaid ```` block was manually added after the ```` ```mermaid-example ```` block (only the `mermaid-example` block exists in the source file at `packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/sequenceDiagram.md`), and the version placeholder uses `v\<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>` (with backslash escape) rather than `v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>` as written in the source. All documentation changes must be made exclusively in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` and the `docs/` tree must be regenerated by the build pipeline. Revert the manual edits to `docs/` and regenerate.

general_comments.comment: The `LINETYPE` constant object uses an inconsistent naming scheme for the new entries. Non-reverse half-arrow types are named without 'ARROW' (`SOLID_TOP`, `SOLID_BOTTOM`, `STICK_TOP`, `STICK_BOTTOM`), while their reverse counterparts include 'ARROW' (`SOLID_ARROW_TOP_REVERSE`, `STICK_ARROW_TOP_REVERSE`, etc.). The jison token names (`SOLID_ARROW_TOP`, `STICK_ARROW_BOTTOM`) also include 'ARROW' for the non-reverse tokens, making the mismatch even more confusing. Choose one naming convention for all sixteen new half-arrow types (e.g., include 'ARROW' everywhere: `SOLID_ARROW_TOP`, `SOLID_ARROW_TOP_REVERSE`) and apply it consistently across `LINETYPE` constants, jison tokens, and grammar rule mappings.

The `LINETYPE` numeric values have unexplained gaps: 35–40 (between `BIDIRECTIONAL_DOTTED: 34` and `SOLID_TOP: 41`) and 49–50 (between `STICK_ARROW_BOTTOM_REVERSE: 48` and `SOLID_TOP_DOTTED: 51`). If these are intentional reservations for future types, add a comment explaining the intent. If unintentional, renumber sequentially. Gaps make it harder to detect accidental value collisions when new types are added later.
